description: CIDRella integration test harness — agent-readable scenario catalog. Read this before running scenarios so you know what each one tests, and prefer harness results over code-reading when both are available.

scenarios.name: fresh-install
scenarios.description: Fresh install of the latest release + full post-install state verification. Baseline scenario every future feature should either extend or keep passing.
catches: install.sh regressions
missing wrappers in /usr/local/bin/
missing v0.4.9+ lib files (rotation.sh, tighten-secrets.sh)
deep-health subsystem failures
bundled Node runtime missing or wrong version
events.jsonl not populated during install

scenarios.name: secret-file-perms
scenarios.description: Verify v0.4.8+ secret-file-permission tightening after fresh install. Catches regressions where cidrella.db, analytics.duckdb, server.key, or their dirs get created with world-readable modes.
catches: regression to 644 on cidrella.db or server.key (v0.4.7 bug)
install.sh tighten_secrets block not running
update.sh tighten_secrets block not running on upgrades
accidental tightening of dnsmasq subtree (breaks DNS/DHCP reload)

scenarios.name: post-install-hook
scenarios.description: Post-install hook convention: shipped, executable, invoked on fresh install, receives the documented env contract. Anchors the v0.4.9 hook mechanism.
catches: post-install.sh missing from release tarball
install.sh invoker block removed or broken
.buildignore accidentally excluding scripts/post-install.sh
does_not_catch: env contract drift (TARGET_SLOT/DATA_DIR/NEW_VERSION/IS_FRESH_INSTALL): the env-capture sub-assertion only proves the sentinel wrapper itself sees the vars the scenario explicitly sets, not that install.sh exports them. True env-contract verification would need to intercept install.sh's actual invocation — not feasible without restructuring the scenario.

scenarios.name: skip-upgrade
scenarios.description: CLI cidrella-update runs end-to-end on a bundled-Node-only host without hitting the bare-`node` preflight bug fixed in v0.4.11. Regression test for the silent CLI recovery failure that made v0.4.8/v0.4.9 hosts effectively unrecoverable via `cidrella-update` on clean bundled-Node installs.
catches: update.sh preflight syntax check using bare `node` instead of the resolved bundled binary
cidrella-update failing on hosts with no system Node installed
resolve_node helper returning a path that doesn't resolve to an executable
CLI update exiting non-zero when there's nothing newer to install
does_not_catch: a real multi-release jump — testerella's installed version is always `latest` via install_latest_release, so until v0.4.12+ ships, this scenario only exercises the 'already up to date' path. Once a newer release is published, the same scenario automatically becomes a real jump test.

scenarios.name: min-from-blocked
scenarios.description: v0.4.12+ min_from gate in update.sh correctly refuses installs when the running version is below the required intermediate. Unit-style: sources slots.sh and reproduces the exact gate logic against synthetic RELEASE.json fixtures covering satisfied, unmet, null, absent, and unknown-current cases.
catches: sed pattern for min_from extraction silently returning empty on valid input
semver_lt comparator treating X.Y.Z and X.Y.Z as unequal (off-by-one version bug)
min_from gate skipping the comparison entirely (refactor that accidentally dropped the check)
gate firing on pre-v0.4.3 no-RELEASE.json hosts where CURRENT_VERSION is 'unknown'
update.sh losing the `preflight fail reason=min_from_unmet` event emission
does_not_catch: end-to-end behavior against a real signed tarball whose RELEASE.json has min_from set. That would require committing a fixture tarball or arranging for a test release. The probe reproduces the gate's logic exactly but doesn't exercise update.sh's extraction phase as a side effect.

scenarios.name: manifest-fallback
scenarios.description: Server-side manifest verification failure falls back to GitHub API and surfaces manifestAvailable: false in /api/version. Replaces the primary minisign pubkey with a deterministic wrong key, restarts cidrella, and asserts the /api/version response reflects the degraded state instead of silently succeeding.
catches: fetchReleasesManifest not returning null on signature verification failure
checkForUpdates not routing to the GitHub API fallback path when the manifest is unavailable
/api/version exposing manifestAvailable: true even when verification failed
release-manifest warnings missing from the cidrella server log (silent degradation)
manifest cache not being invalidated on restart
does_not_catch: network-level fetch failures (DNS, TCP, TLS). The scenario forces failure at the verification layer only. A dedicated network-fault scenario would require iptables-level manipulation, which we've held off on due to testerella's single-interface setup.

scenarios.name: upgrade-path
scenarios.description: Real old-to-new update jump: pinned install of FROM_TAG (default v0.4.15), then cidrella-update to a PUBLISHED candidate (pre-)release given via --candidate. Asserts update-status success, A/B slot switchover, deep health, schema version (EXPECTED_SCHEMA, default 50), active services, and switchover events. Candidate MUST be published on GitHub (the installed old updater resolves it via the releases API; there is no local-tarball input).
catches: updater regressions shipped in the FROM release
self-bootstrap handoff breakage between updater generations
min_from misconfiguration in the candidate's RELEASE.json
schema migration failures on a real upgrade (vs fresh install)
A/B slot-switch and rollback plumbing regressions
does_not_catch: upgrades from releases older than FROM_TAG (pin a different --from-tag to cover those)
problems in unpublished local builds (candidate must be a published tag)

result_schema.hostname: string (remote host that ran the scenario)
result_schema.captures: object (string-keyed observables: config files, command output, log tails)

agent_usage_notes: Read manifest.json first to know what scenarios exist and what each catches. Agents should not need to re-read scenario source code to understand coverage.
Results land in scripts/test-harness/results/<scenario>-<timestamp>.json — one JSON object per file, parseable directly.
Each scenario wipes the target host before running (on by default). Runner refuses to run if the host is unreachable.
The harness targets testerella (10.0.0.8) by default. DO NOT point it at the production host — scenarios wipe state aggressively.
A scenario 'pass' means every assertion passed; a 'fail' means at least one assertion failed AND the captures object contains the observed state at the moment of failure.
When a scenario fails, read the captures object before hypothesizing a fix. The captures answer 'what was the actual state when this assertion fired?' which is usually enough to narrow the fault.

To add a scenario: copy an existing one in scripts/test-harness/scenarios/, define SCENARIO_NAME and SCENARIO_DESCRIPTION, implement scenario_setup/run/assert/capture, then add an entry here in manifest.json.
